statement: A leaking tap drips once every 2 seconds, and 20 drops make 1 millilitre. How many litres of water drip from the tap in one day?

choices.misconception: I worked out the water for one hour, 1800 drops or 90 millilitres, and forgot to multiply by 24.
I counted one drop every second instead of one drop every 2 seconds.
I thought 1 litre is 100 millilitres, so I divided 2160 by 100.
I got 2160 millilitres and forgot to change millilitres into litres.

hints: How many seconds are there in a day?
Check units: go from seconds to drops, from drops to millilitres, then from millilitres to litres. Write the unit after every number so the last step is not skipped.
A day has $24 \times 3600 = 86\,400$ seconds, so there are $43\,200$ drops, which is $43\,200 \div 20 = 2160$ millilitres.

solutions.reliable: A day has $24 \times 60 \times 60 = 86\,400$ seconds. One drop every 2 seconds gives $43\,200$ drops. At 20 drops per millilitre that is $43\,200 \div 20 = 2160$ millilitres. Since 1 litre is 1000 millilitres, this is 2.16 litres. The transferable idea: before bubbling, ask whether the number is in the unit the question asked for.
solutions.elegant: Work per hour to keep the numbers small: 1800 drops, which is 90 millilitres. Per day: $24 \times 90 = 2160$ millilitres, which is 2.16 litres.

whyOnTest: Every step is easy; the marks are lost by stopping at millilitres or at one hour, so this tests the final units check.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
